{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past interactions as broad, continuing interest in related products or media, with insufficient attention to the specific purpose of the next choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they connect to a specific recurring interest, such as a familiar artist, a preferred musical sound, or a recognizable story theme.",
    "Complementary supplies and accessories align when they serve an identifiable task supported by recent purchases."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with stronger matches despite requiring different tasks, equipment, sounds, or viewing interests.",
    "Past ownership is treated as continuing demand for similar devices or supplies, overlooking existing coverage and uncertain replacement needs.",
    "Historical interactions appear to carry more certainty about lasting preferences and current needs than the feedback supports."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared product domain, brand, ecosystem, musical era, or broad genre substitutes for a specific reason to choose an item.",
    "Surface similarities such as compilation format, accessory type, or general workshop usefulness generate matches across materially different purposes."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent and repeated interactions help distinguish current tasks, seasonal interests, and desired musical intensity from older, isolated activity.",
    "Exact compatibility, intended material, connector, dimensions, and equipment requirements determine whether related products are useful.",
    "Complementing existing possessions differs from duplicating them, just as matching an artist or genre differs from matching the desired album, repertoire, or sound."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top-ranked items often share a broad association with history without offering the specific relevance, compatibility, or added usefulness needed to motivate a choice now.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked recommendations users accept for a concrete connection to a recent or repeated interest, measured separately by category.",
    "The frequency of rejections attributed to unrelated tasks, incompatible requirements, duplicated functions, or mismatched media style.",
    "The frequency of recommendations whose relevance users cannot assess from identifiable item content, tracked separately from explicit preference mismatches."
  ]
}
